# RTX 2080 Ti ARC versus complete semantic matrix

User authority: compare ordinary single/multi-agent workloads, ARC versus full semantic eviction and prefetch, record relevant metrics and recommend next work. The user selected the repository's representative workloads. These are generated sessions, not production traces.

Primary comparison: Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, dense FP16, TP1, eager, Triton attention, ordinary FP16 math, V2 runner, mapped pinned WSL memory. Three seeds (1103, 2207, 3301); two workloads; ARC and complete mean-semantic eviction plus causal tool-wait semantic prefetch. Within each workload/seed, alternate arm order ARC/semantic, semantic/ARC, ARC/semantic. One fresh server per run; one identical warmup excluded from load metrics; no source or configuration tuning after valid measurements.

Single-agent: the first repository session, six growing-context turns, plus twelve independent open-loop background requests. Multi-agent: six sessions, with the repository's one abandonment after three completed turns, plus the same twelve background requests (45 completed requests). Generated private tool waits are exposed only when elapsed; policy sees the completed initial exact prefix and a fixed 250ms wait estimate, never actual future waits, content, or abandonment. Agent release depends on prior completion; cache/batch/arrival histories may differ across policies.

Equal memory geometry: 640 GPU blocks and 199 CPU blocks, 16 tokens per block; 280 MiB GPU KV and 87.0625 MiB CPU KV for this model. Max 8192 model tokens, max three running sequences, max 1024 batched tokens. Main admission threshold2 in both arms. Full semantic: real SemanticPolicy, mean keys/heads, alpha0.5/default blend, continuous synchronous flat scoring, stride1, semantic selector, 5% staging cap inside the same GPU pool. Safe prefix-preserving staging enabled; native adoption disabled because its BF16 guard excludes this host's required FP16. No future labels or invented semantic scores. ARC: stock ARC policy via shared connector/event instrumentation, capture/scoring disabled by the normal instrumentation-only configuration, no speculative staging.

Headline runs keep component profiler off. Passive manager method timing/counters, sampled pool observations, required preservation/transfer events, client timestamps, and external 250ms CPU/RSS/NVML samples remain enabled in both arms. Observation overhead is included and can differ with event volume. Do not label these uninstrumented production benchmarks.

Separate diagnostic matrix: one pair per workload, seed1103, identical geometry/threshold2, component profiler and additional runner/capture aggregate timers enabled. Exclude from headline serving aggregates. Deferred sampled CUDA stream durations overlap host/transfer/model work and must not be summed. Explicit post-load fence/flush is outside client timing. No per-step device synchronization.

Conditional admission-stress supplement: if the primary matrix has no CPU eviction or no consumed prefetch, run one matched threshold0 pair per workload at seed1103. Keep workload and memory unchanged. This deliberately removes the admission guard to expose cache contention; it is a diagnostic, not a replacement for ordinary threshold2 results or a new product default. Preserve unfavorable results.

Metrics: successful/failed requests and exact output tokens; release- and submit-to-first-token mean/median/p90/p95/max with sample counts and descriptive tail caveats; intertoken intervals (network chunks may contain multiple tokens); per-request elapsed; completed output tokens / intended load-start to last completion; background and agent/session breakdowns and completion tails; client release lateness; GPU-local hits, external restoration, actual prompt execution; H2D, D2H, staging/splice traffic and existing worker transfer timings; successful/failing transfer jobs, readiness versus consumption/fences, unused staging; CPU admissions/evictions, lookup results, semantic score updates and eviction activation, constrained prefetch competition; sampled CPU residency/GPU pool use; CUDA allocated/reserved load peaks; sampled process CPU seconds/RSS byte-seconds/peak RSS and device utilization/power/temperature. Missing or unsupported measurements remain null with explanations. Whole-device samples include display/other activity; RSS across processes can double-count shared mappings. No dollar-cost, capacity frontier, or exclusive kernel-time claim.

Validity: preserve full prompt/output token lists and ordered native key evidence. Fixed PYTHONHASHSEED; compare exact paired prompts/outputs/key chains, disclose numerical divergence rather than dropping it. Validate configured manager/policy classes and observed semantic capture/scoring; report zeros honestly. Native transfer records and worker completion precede reuse. No elapsed-time inference substituted for actual activation.

Runtime: installed prerelease wheel plus a task-local four-module overlay from the retained wait-hint runtime and the reviewed companion block-pool publication patch. The forwarding diff consists only of the previously used wait-hint methods. Native adoption stays disabled for FP16; the fifth module supplies the API required by the existing CPU tests. Shared runtime and source stay unchanged. Preserve pins, commands, protocol, per-request/aggregate CSV and JSON, component exports and losslessly compressed logs.

Operational choices: run serially on the idle GPU under the project lock, finite 600s client-load deadline and 180s readiness deadline per lifecycle; supervise and stop only owned descendants. These finite coverage/deadline choices are assistant engineering bounds, not user-imposed limits. No commits or pushes. Apply storage-steward at handback; retain useful model caches and evidence, remove disposable task bytecode/scratch after recoverability checks.

Pre-primary compatibility decision: the optional batch-invariant linear kernel passed a tiny exactness check, but the separate 0.5B serving pilot ran around 1.3 tokens/s instead of the ordinary path's roughly 25 tokens/s. Main cells use the normal non-batch-invariant FP16 path in both arms. Exact cross-arm output checks are retained; any numerical/batching divergence will be disclosed and investigated rather than assumed to be cache corruption or silently omitted. This decision precedes all valid 1.5B measurements.
